title: Design System: Dota 2 Private Lobby Statistics

display.purpose: KPI values, spotlight name, profile name; always with tabular figures.

title.purpose: Row and column leaders inside tables and leaderboards.

body.purpose: Prose, table cells, error copy; captions step down to 12-13px in ash grey.

label.purpose: Table headers, badges, nav items, KPI labels, tags.

shadows.name: card-resting
shadows.purpose: Default flat-on-the-page shadow for cards and leaderboard tiles, plus a 1px inner top highlight.

shadows.name: card-hover
shadows.purpose: Faint azure bloom added as a card lifts 3px on hover.

shadows.name: brand-mark
shadows.purpose: The one colored glow; belongs to the header logo only.

shadows.name: medal
shadows.purpose: Separates the circular podium badge from the leaderboard row behind it.

shadows.name: tile-hover
shadows.purpose: Accent-tinted lift for hero tiles and stat tiles.

motion.name: ease-rise
motion.purpose: Entrance rise-in for cards and leaderboard tiles, and bar fill.

motion.name: state-fast
motion.purpose: Color, background-color, and border-color changes on nav and inputs.

motion.name: state-mid
motion.purpose: Transform and box-shadow changes on card, leaderboard, and hero-tile hover.

motion.name: rise-in
motion.purpose: Section entrance; 65ms / 130ms stagger for the 2nd and 3rd grid children.

motion.name: bar-fill
motion.purpose: Progress and split bars filling from the left.

motion.name: ambient-drift
motion.purpose: Slow drift of the two background radial gradients.

narrative.overview:
This is a ledger before it is a dashboard. The group's shared match history is the product, and the interface behaves like a well-kept record book that happens to be alive: a near-black page, generous rounded panels laid out in a calm grid, and every number set in tabular figures so columns line up the way a handwritten ledger would. Hero art, medals, and colored meters are the illustrations in the margins - they give the book its world without ever competing with the figures.

The density is middle-of-the-road and deliberate. Cards are large and padded, sections are separated by a consistent 26px rhythm, and the whole thing stays legible on a phone without collapsing into a list. Depth is tonal at rest: the page is obsidian-canvas, cards are charcoal-panel, inner wells step up to charcoal-panel-2 and -3. A single soft shadow and a 3px hover lift are the only structural motion the surfaces themselves perform.

The atmosphere is calm and precise, with a quiet competitive edge underneath. Radiant and Dire are always present as the two data poles, leaderboards use real medal tiers, and the eye is trained to read rank first and value second. Nothing shouts; the numbers are trusted, so the design does not need to sell them.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black canvas with large, softly shadowed rounded panels.
Sentence-case Sora headings over Inter body and tabular-figure numbers.
Radiant azure and Dire gold as the two semantic data poles.
Gold reserved for earned achievement (rank 1, medals, leading values).
Hero art used as spotlight and tile imagery, never as background noise.
One hover lift everywhere; one soft card shadow; no elevation ladder.

rules.name: The Earned Gold Rule
rules.body: Dire gold is payment, not paint. It is allowed on medal tiers, pill-value leaders, the MVP marker, and the Dire side of a split - and nowhere else. If gold is decorative, it is wrong.

rules.name: The Radiant/Dire Rule
rules.body: Radiant is azure and Dire is gold, always, in that pairing. This deliberately does not mirror the in-game team colors; it maps the two sides onto the system's cool/warm accent pair so a split bar reads instantly in a dark UI.

rules.name: The Token Rule
rules.body: Never hardcode a color; reference a token. Every value above exists as a CSS custom property in web/src/styles.css.

rules.name: The Sentence-Case Rule
rules.body: Headings and labels are sentence case. Uppercase is never used to signal hierarchy - weight and size carry it.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number that can appear in a column or a ranking is set with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums. Figures must align vertically; the ledger depends on it.

rules.name: The One Lift Rule
rules.body: A surface lifts exactly once, by 3px, on hover. No static elevation hierarchy, no stacked shadows, no parallax.

rules.name: The Respectful Motion Rule
rules.body: Every animation is disabled or reduced under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, including the lift transform and the ambient background drift.

rules.name: The Others Rule
rules.body: A share chart names at most five slices. Everything past that is one neutral Others slice that states how many heroes it stands for, so the chart never renders more arcs than it can label - whether the group has eighteen heroes or eight hundred.

rules.name: The Column-Truth Rule
rules.body: A date sits in the column of its real weekday, computed from the date itself. A calendar that is one day off still looks tidy, so it is validated against real dates, never by eye.

dos: Do reference a token for every color, radius, and shadow; the token set lives in web/src/styles.css and the design-system skill documents it.
Do set every column, rank, and KPI figure in tabular-nums, and give numeric columns text-align: right.
Do reserve dire-gold for earned gold: medal tiers, pill-value, the MVP marker, and the Dire side of a split.
Do keep Radiant = azure and Dire = gold as a fixed pairing in every split, legend, and dot.
Do use sentence case for headings and labels, and let size and weight carry hierarchy.
Do keep one hover lift (3px on cards and leaderboard tiles, 4px on hero tiles) and reduce all motion under prefers-reduced-motion.
Do fall back to a tinted initials avatar whenever hero art is missing or fails to load.
Do treat a leaderboard card header as navigation: the title plus a chevron, with a static title when the board has no entries so the card never looks clickable and does nothing.
Do keep a category's metric as the first numeric column, in tabular figures, and keep it on screen at phone width.
Do reserve the gold pill-value for winning values (>=50%); a 0% entry is plain text.
Do treat an optional payload as optional: a missing matches.json becomes one explanatory line, never an error page or an empty-looking block.
Do give every chart a role="img" text alternative and repeat its numbers as text; a chart summarises, it never replaces the table.
Do color a hero's chart slice with the same tint as its tile, by reading one shared helper over one ordering.
Do bucket every date by the reader's local time zone and assert each calendar cell against the real weekday of its date.
donts: Don't hardcode a hex in a component; if a value is missing, add it to @theme first.
Don't use victory green or defeat red for anything other than win/loss and error semantics.
Don't use uppercase, letter-spaced headings as a hierarchy device.
Don't nest cards inside cards - panels hold content, and depth is expressed by the panel ramp instead.
Don't introduce a second resting shadow or a static elevation ladder; one shadow, one hover lift.
Don't use gold or a hero tint as a general-purpose highlight; both are earned or attached to a specific entity.
Don't ship a control that looks interactive but has no action - a header affordance either navigates or is not rendered.
Don't add decorative gradients, glows, or bounce/elastic easing outside the existing ambient background drift.
